OTT Releases This Week (18 May - 24 May 2026): ‘Desi Bling’, ‘System’ And More Movies And Web Shows Releasing On Streaming Platforms
From Sonakshi Sinha’s courtroom drama ‘System’ to the glamorous reality series ‘Desi Bling’, here are the biggest OTT releases arriving this week across streaming platforms with action, mystery, comedy and drama for every viewer.
Rishika SinghMay 18, 2026, 14:07 IST




​The third week of May brings a busy and varied OTT line-up, with platform releases ranging from sharp courtroom drama to glossy reality entertainment and high-stakes thrillers. The mix feels broad enough to suit viewers looking for something serious, something breezy or something with a bit of both. What stands out this week is how different these titles are in tone and texture. Some lean on star power, others on mood and mystery, but each one has enough going for it to make the watchlist feel fuller than usual.

System

Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari’s System arrives on Amazon Prime Video on May 22, 2026, Sonakshi Sinha and Jyotika at the centre of a courtroom story built on privilege, pressure and quiet conflict. Sonakshi plays an ambitious public prosecutor who is chasing a crucial run of wins, while Jyotika brings a sharper, more grounded presence to the case. The film looks set to work as both a legal drama and a character study.

Desi Bling

Netflix will stream Desi Bling from May 20, 2026 turning the spotlight on Indian expats in Dubai and their polished, high-energy world. With Karan Kundrra and Tejasswi Prakash among the familiar faces, the series promises glamour, personal drama and the kind of social dynamics that reality TV thrives on. It is designed to give viewers plenty of sparkle with the inevitable emotional spillover.

Tom Clancy’s Jack Ryan: Ghost War

Amazon Prime Video brings Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan: Ghost War on May 20,2026 with John Krasinski returning to a dangerous mission after stepping away from active fieldwork. The series brings back the familiar mix of covert operations, betrayal and international danger, with a new conspiracy that forces Ryan to depend on old allies and new instincts.

The Boroughs

Netflix releases The Boroughs on May 21, 2026 and the show shifts into eerie territory, with Alfred Molina leading the story of a widower who discovers something deeply unsettling in a retirement community. Backed by the Duffer Brothers, the show blends supernatural suspense with an unusual setting, giving the mystery a slower, stranger kind of menace.

Madhuvidhu

SonyLIV will stream Madhuvidhu on May 22, and this Malayalam romantic comedy follows a young man whose search for marriage is complicated by family superstition and everyday chaos. Sharafudheen leads the film with Kalyani Panicker, while veteran comedians add the kind of comic timing that gives the story warmth and pace.

Ladies First

Netflix releases Ladies First on May 22, bringing Sacha Baron Cohen into a sharply flipped world where gender roles have been completely reversed. The film follows a powerful man who suddenly finds himself in a reality where women hold the reins and men are pushed to the margins. With Rosamund Pike also part of the cast, the film blends satire, social commentary and broad comedy in a way that should make it stand out from the week’s line-up.

Lee Cronin’s The Mummy

Lee Cronin’s The Mummy arrives on May 19 and will be available to buy and rent on Prime Video, Apple TV and Google Play. The film takes a familiar horror concept and gives it a more intimate, unsettling edge. The story follows a journalist and his wife as they search for their missing daughter, only to stumble into something far more frightening in the Egyptian desert. Jack Reynor leads the cast, with Laia Costa, May Calamawy and Verónica Falcón adding to the tension.

Satrangi: Badle Ka Khel

ZEE5 will stream Satrangi: Badle Ka Khel on May 22 with Anshumaan Pushkar stars in this revenge-driven series set in rural Uttar Pradesh, where identity, caste and power shape every move. The show uses performance and secrecy as part of its emotional pull, making the revenge arc feel rooted in a much larger social world.

This week’s OTT slate is less about one big title and more about range. The strongest draw is the variety itself, with each project offering a different mood and a different kind of engagement. For viewers, that usually means one thing: there is plenty worth queuing up.
